phase3_findings.description: The added test comment at lib/test/run.sh (diff lines 94-96) states that an uppercase `AUTHORIZATION: BASIC` header is what actions/checkout persists and that matching only the keyword's first letter let that credential through. False against HEAD: this repo's own mirror of that surface, scripts/refresh-app-credentials.sh, writes `AUTHORIZATION: basic ${b64}` (lowercase scheme), and scripts/scrub-credentials.sh's own header note scopes the uppercase claim to the header NAME, not the scheme keyword. The defensible motivation is other producers that emit BASIC/BEARER, which is what the new fixtures actually exercise.

phase3_findings.description:
Narrowing relative to origin/main: the old bracket expressions carried a literal `\` as a class member, so ANY backslash inside a token was consumed; the new alternation admits only the two escape units `/` and `\`, so any other backslash sequence (`
`, `	`, `\uXXXX`, `"`) terminates the match. Measured: `AUTHORIZATION: basic QUJDRA
RUZHSA==` redacts fully on origin/main but leaves the tail on HEAD, and `AUTHORIZATION: basic AB
SECRETTAILXYZ` (fewer than four units before the backslash, so the `{4,}` floor is never reached) is not redacted at all. The agent graded this Suggestion because the four documented shapes are base64/base64url, whose alphabets contain no backslash, so the only escape a conforming token can carry is `/` — which the change handles.
phase3_findings.counter_evidence: The final-pass reviewer examined this same class independently and judged it not a new fail-open: a lone `\` mid-token now terminates the match exactly as whitespace and every other non-class byte always did, and a raw backslash is not a member of any base64/base64url credential alphabet. The two agents disagree on framing, not on the measured behavior. The scrub is documented as an incomplete blocklist (`scrub.blocklist_incomplete: true`).
phase3_findings.fix_recommendation: Optional and non-blocking: either generalize the escape unit to `\\.` (any escaped character) in both groups, or leave as-is — the changeset already discloses the narrowing.

report:
## Verdict: APPROVE with notes (the #1915 fix is correct, mutation-verified discriminating, and satisfies all five acceptance criteria; four Suggestions and one advisory remain, none of which gates merge at the configured `critical` threshold)

## Issue Compliance
Reviewed against issue #1915: The credential scrub eats the JSON escape backslash, so large execution transcripts are unparseable — criteria from workpad; scope unchanged. Requirement-based checklist items are included in the verification results below.
Criteria came from the `/prflow:implement` workpad comment — this run's authoritative set, possibly narrowed from the issue.
No divergence between the workpad's criteria and the issue body's.

All five acceptance criteria verify PASS (VC-8 through VC-12), each established empirically rather than from the author's account.

## Verification Checklist Results
12 passed, 0 failed, 0 inconclusive — 0 via lite probe, 12 via agent.

- VC-1: NORMALIZED (wording-only) — the generated claim predicted that `\/` leaves a lone backslash unmatched mid-token; the verifier measured the opposite (the `\\` branch matches a lone backslash by itself, `/` is already a class member), so the mismatch is in the generated wording and the code is correct [scripts/scrub-credentials.sh:64]

<details><summary>Passed items (11 of 12) — click to expand</summary>

- VC-2: BSD `sed -E` on macOS supports `(...){4,}` on a parenthesized alternation — verified against the real BSD binary [scripts/scrub-credentials.sh:64]
- VC-3: `\1` still refers to the header-name group after the token alternation became group 2 [scripts/scrub-credentials.sh:64-65]
- VC-4: both universals in the new header comment falsification-tested by mutating copies — widening to a bare `\` corrupts the JSON escape, relaxing `{4,}` to `+` eats the recorded `//` [scripts/scrub-credentials.sh:57-59]
- VC-5: the four-unit floor behaves as the changeset states (3 units left alone, 4 units redacted, both rules); no realistic credential shape falls under it [.changeset/issue-1915-scrub-escape-backslash.md]
- VC-6: `$SCR` (18176) and `$DEN_JQ` (18174) are bound above the new block and never reassigned [lib/test/run.sh:18174]
- VC-7: the `"1915"` run_sh_blocks entry satisfies coverage_map_guard.py's shape rules; the guard and the retention check both exit 0 [lib/test/modules/coverage-map.json:1514]
- VC-8: a JSON document carrying a `basic` credential still parses after scrubbing [scripts/scrub-credentials.sh:65]
- VC-9: the same holds for the `Bearer` rule with a non-GitHub token [scripts/scrub-credentials.sh:64]
- VC-10: `sed 's/AUTHORIZATION: basic //'` round-trips with its trailing `//'` intact [lib/test/run.sh:18318]
- VC-11: the round-trip test sits in the run.sh region the coverage map labels `#1064 D4`, embeds all four shapes, and asserts both parseability and full byte equality [lib/test/run.sh:18307-18318]

## Code Review Findings

### Suggestion / Minor

1. The added test comment stating that an uppercase `AUTHORIZATION: BASIC` header is what actions/checkout persists, and that matching only the keyword's first letter let that credential through, is false against HEAD: scripts/refresh-app-credentials.sh writes `AUTHORIZATION: basic ${b64}` (lowercase scheme), and scrub-credentials.sh's own header note scopes the uppercase claim to the header NAME. The pre-fix `[Bb]asic` already matched checkout's header; the real motivation is other producers emitting BASIC/BEARER, which is what the new fixtures exercise. (raised by 1/4 agents) [filed Important by comment-analyzer; capped to Suggestion by the Phase 4.1.5 behavior-inert prose cap — first conjunct: the subject is the sentence, not the mechanism's coverage, and the per-letter classes are correct either way; limb one: no tool parses this comment to decide behavior (no declaration marker, no shellcheck/type directive; the pin-corpus lint reads prose only to assert prose); limb two: `.github/actions/vendor-plugin/vendor-slice.sh` prunes the whole `lib/test` subtree with `rm -rf "$stage/lib/test"`, so it reaches no consumer checkout and is published nowhere]
2. The two new assertion names read `an uppercase BASIC/BEARER scheme keyword is STILL redacted`; `still` implies the uppercase form was already redacted, whereas this diff's rewrite is what first makes it so. (raised by 1/4 agents)
3. Narrowing relative to origin/main: the old bracket expressions carried a literal `\` as a class member, so any backslash inside a token was consumed; the new alternation admits only `\/` and `\\`, so any other escape (`\n`, `\t`, `\uXXXX`, `\"`) terminates the match — and where fewer than four units precede the backslash the `{4,}` floor is never reached and nothing is redacted at all. The filing agent graded it Suggestion because the four documented shapes are base64/base64url, whose alphabets contain no backslash. The final-pass reviewer examined the same class independently and judged it not a new fail-open, since a lone `\` now terminates the match exactly as every other non-class byte always did. (raised by 1/4 agents)
4. The acceptance criterion names the `#1064 D4` block; the new assertions land beside the existing `scrub-credentials:` assertions roughly 95 lines above the `D4/AC8: scrub-transcript.sh arms` heading. Not an AC failure — `#1064 D4` is the coverage map's own label for scripts/scrub-credentials.sh, and VC-11 confirmed the block sits in exactly that region — but a later reader reconciling AC to test may trip over the literal wording. (raised by 1/4 agents)

1. Advisory, non-blocking (repo review prompt extension): neither durable surface carries a `Verification evidence:` marker — issue #1915's workpad has none and the PR description has none.
